rulings.challenge_claim: A ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed at MT 1:5, and the rescue-formula recurrence the row builds on is asserted with neither a tier label nor a book-wide digit.
rulings.grounds: Both prongs verify from bytes. MT 1:5 carries one of the book's variant notes and the doublet stands openly in the verse's own bytes, unpointed beside pointed: אצורך אֶצָּרְךָ֤ (oshb:Jer.1.5, byte tier). The row argues that verse's appointment content and lists it as evidence, while its disclosure sentence covers only the parashah layer; the three parashah citations it does make are all correct as to type and verse (setumah at MT 1:3, petuchah after MT 1:6 and after MT 1:10, tier-3 weak, single-witness), so the layer was read and the variant layer was not. Span-relevant mark disclosure is unconditional, so the omission stands on the rule alone. Second, the recurrence sentence pairing web:Jer.1.8 with web:Jer.1.19 carries no tier and no digit. Re-derived: the byte-identical core of the pair is כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier), which stands at 4 verses book-wide at byte tier (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Jer.1.8, oshb:Jer.1.19, oshb:Jer.15.20, oshb:Jer.30.11; 5 verses at skeleton tier, adding oshb:Jer.46.28), so the bracket is real but not distinctive to this chapter; and the two rescue infinitives differ in spelling, defective לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier; sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) against plene לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). The challenge's digits reproduce exactly for the objects its sentences name. The row's own hedge that the clause recurs in close wording is byte-appropriate and should survive; only the tier label and the digit are missing. New finding in the same disclosure class: one paseq seg falls at MT 1:10, inside the span, and is likewise undisclosed.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add a variant-note disclosure for oshb:Jer.1.5 (single-witness), naming the note and quoting the pointed reading the argument relies on, spliced from source at byte tier; add the paseq seg at MT 1:10 as a count-only single-witness disclosure with no intra-verse position claim. In the same field, keep the close-wording hedge but tier-label the recurrence and attach the swept object and digit (the byte-identical three-word core, byte tier, 4 verses book-wide) and name the two infinitive spellings. Test the cure must pass: a span-relevant mark-disclosure sweep over the variant and paseq inventories returns clean for Jer.1.4-Jer.1.10, and the recurrence sentence carries an object-named, digit-bearing citation with its tier - the two things whose absence killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: An unbroken divine speech runs across the row's own close undisclosed, the close warrant rests on a form label the pointed bytes do not carry, and the northern-invader motif is anchored on the wrong verse without a sweep digit.
rulings.grounds: The first prong holds and is the substantive finding: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.1.14, byte tier) opens a divine speech, and MT 1:15 through MT 1:19 add no further speech introduction, no word-event formula and no change of speaker - a byte-true frame continuity crossing this unit's own close at MT 1:16 / MT 1:17 that the row nowhere discloses, where a device straddling a row's seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. It does not follow that the cut is wrong: the turn at MT 1:17 moves the address from the northern kingdoms back to the prophet and puts a second-person charge on him, which is a licensed participant-shift ground. The second prong is real but mis-framed. The bytes at MT 1:17 read וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier), an emphatic pronoun before a second-person prefix conjugation continued by waw-perfects, not the imperative form the book uses at its discourse frames (שִׁמְע֥וּ at oshb:Jer.2.4; רְא֣וּ at oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier), and the second witness renders a command. The row's own wording is a construction label, not a form claim, so the defect is a missing form disclosure rather than a false form label - a low-severity precision gap, not a warrant failure. The third prong is likewise refined. The phrase the row anchors is מַמְלְכ֥וֹת צָפ֖וֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.15, byte tier), which is unique to that verse (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier), so the parenthetical is right for that object; but the north enters the unit two verses earlier at צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier; sweep: 5 verses, skeleton tier, against 20 verses for the contiguous northern skeleton), so calling the motif introduced at the later verse mis-anchors it inside the unit's own span. What is defective without qualification is that the recurrence sentence carries no tier, no digit and no verse anchors for the material it says the motif recurs across. New finding in the disclosure class: three paseq segs over two verses (MT 1:13 and MT 1:15) sit inside the span undisclosed.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure that the divine speech introduced at oshb:Jer.1.14 continues past this unit's close with no fresh speech frame, and state what carries the cut instead (the participant turn back to the prophet at oshb:Jer.1.17); re-cut the motif sentence so it names its swept object and digit (the kingdoms-of-the-north phrase, skeleton tier, 1 verse, at oshb:Jer.1.15) and records the north's first site at oshb:Jer.1.13, replacing the unanchored scope phrase with verse anchors and a tier; add the paseq segs at MT 1:13 and MT 1:15 as count-only single-witness disclosure. boundary_rationale: keep the close warrant and add a one-sentence form disclosure at oshb:Jer.1.17 that the shape is a prefix conjugation after an emphatic pronoun carrying imperatival force in both witnesses. Test the cure must pass: a cross-seam cohesion check finds no undisclosed byte-true device straddling this unit's close; every motif and recurrence sentence names its swept object, its unit and a digit with its tier; the mark-disclosure sweep is clean for paseq across Jer.1.13-Jer.1.16.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's stated boundary warrant, that its closing clause is the same rescue clause as the one at web:Jer.1.8, overstates the byte relationship and is contested at byte level; and the span continues a divine speech opened three verses before its onset without disclosure, with gloss extent parting from splice extent in both directions and a unit_type carrying no narrative verb.
rulings.grounds: Both challenge items land on the same core defect and it is upheld: the two clauses are not the same. The bytes read כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier) against כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י נְאֻם יְהוָ֖ה לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier) - the postpositive formula stands after the infinitive at the first site and before it at the second, and the infinitive is defective at the first (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) against plene at the second (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). Only the three-word core is byte-identical, and it stands at 4 verses book-wide at byte tier. The overclaim is load-bearing rather than decorative, because the row's own rejected alternative concedes the onset carries no word-event formula and rests the fresh-unit case on this bracket. Distinct and also upheld: the divine speech introduced at וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.1.14, byte tier) runs into and through this span with no fresh speech frame, an undisclosed continuity at the row's own front seam. Distinct and also upheld: gloss extent misses splice extent in both directions - the five-token closing splice is rendered by a two-word gloss covering only its last word, and the three-token onset splice is glossed by a rendering whose final word renders וְקַמְתָּ֙ (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier), which lies outside the splice. One object correction: the closing splice is five tokens, not four; the extent defect stands regardless. On the unit label, the finding is real but reframed: Jer.1.17-Jer.1.19 carries no narrative verb - every clause sits inside the divine address - so the chosen type is an operative-category deviation, which the closed vocabulary permits only with a one-sentence disclosure. Declared false-positive check, independently verified rather than accepted: the orphan warn on the web:Jer.1.4 evidence ref is a genuine false positive, since the prose argues the bracketed call narrative and that verse is the narrative's own onset; over-listing is the safe direction. Both splices in the row re-collate at byte tier.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the same-clause identity claim with a byte-true recurrence statement that names the byte-identical core, its tier and its digit, and names the inverted formula order and the defective/plene infinitive pair; re-cut the closing gloss so it covers the whole spliced run, or shorten the splice to the glossed word; re-cut the onset gloss so it stops before the word rendering the waw-perfect, or extend the splice to include that word. device_notes: disclose the divine speech continuing from oshb:Jer.1.14 across this unit's front seam and state what carries the cut instead; add the one-sentence operative-category disclosure for a unit label applied to a span with no narrative verb. Test the cure must pass: the recurrence claim re-collates only at the tier it names and its digit reproduces for the object the sentence names; gloss extent equals splice extent at both sites; the cross-seam device is disclosed - the three tests the original failed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row asserts a go-and-proclaim frame and carries a substrate signal for it but never quotes that form, and the splice it does give starts after the frame and stops inside a construct chain that its gloss then completes.
rulings.grounds: Verified from bytes. MT 2:2 opens הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ בְאָזְנֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier), and the row's splice begins three words later at כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) - so the frame the row names in prose, and carries as a substrate signal, has no quoted form anywhere in the row, while a boundary-relevant original-language claim must quote the form it argues. The head pair stands at 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, the other outside this part); its pointed shape is an infinitive absolute followed by a waw-prefixed perfect rather than the imperative form, and the second witness renders it as a command, so the label is functional and the row does not mark it as such. Extent misses run both ways inside the splice the row does give: it ends on the construct אַהֲבַ֖ת (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) while the gloss supplied for it requires the following word כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier), which lies outside the splice, and the messenger formula standing inside the splice is left unglossed. Everything else on the row verifies: the onset splice at oshb:Jer.2.1 re-collates at byte tier as the fourth of the book's twenty-one word-event sites, the formula's mouth is named as divine, and both parashah citations are correct as to type and verse (petuchah at MT 1:19 before the span, petuchah at MT 2:3 at its close, tier-3 weak, single-witness); no variant note and no paseq seg falls in Jer.2.1-Jer.2.3, so nothing further is owed there. Support-audit note: the frame words are byte-present in the verse, so collating them against source proves nothing about this row, whose splice does not contain them - a check of the verse is not a check of the splice.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the opening splice so it begins at the go-and-proclaim pair, spliced programmatically from source at byte tier under its oshb:Jer.2.2 ref, so the named frame and the substrate-signal key have a quoted form behind them; re-cut the gloss to the splice's exact extent, covering the messenger formula and ending where the splice ends, or extend the splice through the following construct member so the existing gloss is covered; add a one-sentence form disclosure that the head shape is an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect construction with imperatival force in both witnesses. Test the cure must pass: every form named in prose or in a substrate-signal key appears in a byte-tier splice under its own witness ref, and gloss extent equals splice extent - the two tests the original failed.

rulings.challenge_claim: One internal rib-pattern element is mislabelled - the contention formula at web:Jer.2.9 is called a verdict when it is the lawsuit's own opening declaration; and the internal-cohesion sentence denying any fresh imperative or formula before Jer.2.14 is refuted by the messenger formula standing verse-initially at oshb:Jer.2.5 and by the imperative chains in two verses the row itself cites as evidence.
rulings.grounds: The two items are distinct defects and both are upheld on bytes. First: MT 2:9 reads לָכֵ֗ן עֹ֛ד אָרִ֥יב אִתְּכֶ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אָרִֽיב (oshb:Jer.2.9, byte tier) - a first-person announcement of continued contention, the dispute verb standing twice and extended to the next generations, with no sentence pronounced; what follows in the span is evidentiary (the witness summonses at MT 2:10 and MT 2:12) and the span closes on the twin-evil charge at MT 2:13, so no verdict stands anywhere in Jer.2.4-Jer.2.13 and the genre element is mistyped. Second and distinct: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.2.5, byte tier) stands verse-initially inside the span (sweep: 2 verses in this chapter for that formula, against 152 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and imperative chains stand at עִבְר֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י כִתִּיִּים֙ וּרְא֔וּ וְקֵדָ֛ר שִׁלְח֥וּ וְהִֽתְבּוֹנְנ֖וּ (oshb:Jer.2.10, byte tier) and שֹׁ֥מּוּ שָׁמַ֖יִם עַל זֹ֑את וְשַׂעֲר֛וּ חָרְב֥וּ (oshb:Jer.2.12, byte tier), the second turning to the heavens as addressee - both verses cited by the row as its own witness-summons evidence. The universal negative is therefore contradicted from inside the row's own evidence set, and it is the sentence carrying the unit's cohesion. The seam itself survives: the messenger formula's mouth is divine and unchanged, so under the ruled granularity it does not cut, and the imperatives are the lawsuit's summons device rather than fresh discourse frames - but that is the disposition the row owed and did not give, and instead it denied the formula outright. The onset splice at oshb:Jer.2.4 re-collates at byte tier and the parashah statement is exact (petuchah at MT 2:3 before the span; the layer silent inside Jer.2.4-Jer.2.13). New finding in the disclosure class: two paseq segs (MT 2:5 and MT 2:13) sit inside the span undisclosed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: retype the MT 2:9 element as the lawsuit's contention announcement rather than a verdict, and re-cut the rib-element list so no element is named that the span's bytes do not carry; replace the sentence denying any fresh imperative or formula with the per-term disposition the cut rule requires - the verse-initial messenger formula at oshb:Jer.2.5 relayed in the same divine mouth with no frame-owner change, and the witness-summons imperatives at oshb:Jer.2.10 and oshb:Jer.2.12 sounding inside the lawsuit rather than opening a fresh discourse frame. device_notes: add the paseq segs at MT 2:5 and MT 2:13 as count-only single-witness disclosure with no intra-verse position claim. Test the cure must pass: every negative sentence in the row survives a byte sweep of the row's own cited verses, and every named genre element matches the bytes at the verse it names - the two tests that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The entry seam at Jer.2.14 rests on a rhetorical-mode observation rather than one of the book's tier-1 seam classes and the closer formula-adjacent rival close is never weighed; and six ketiv/qere verses fall inside the span undisclosed while the blanket denial of any discourse imperative or addressee shift is refuted by the bytes, with a title-stack sentence that blends two distinct objects and quotes neither.
rulings.grounds: Disclosure, upheld and unconditional: six of the book's variant verses, carrying six notes, fall inside Jer.2.14-Jer.2.30 - MT 2:15, 2:16, 2:20, 2:24, 2:25, 2:27 - and none is disclosed. Two of them carry clauses the row argues and lists as evidence: נפשו נַפְשָׁהּ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.24, byte tier) and ילדתני יְלִדְתָּ֔נוּ (oshb:Jer.2.27, byte tier), unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere in each. One refinement: the row's engagement with those two verses is a bare motif label rather than a reading of the disputed forms, so the omission stands on the symmetry duty rather than on any mis-glossed variant. One paseq seg (MT 2:24) is undisclosed in the same class - a new finding. Denial, upheld on two of its four terms: no word-event formula falls inside the span (the formula's sites in these chapters are MT 1:4, 1:11, 1:13 and 2:1) and the chapter's only two messenger-formula verses both fall outside it, so those two terms hold; but addressee shifts stand. The span opens in the third person about Israel at MT 2:14, turns to feminine singular by עָזְבֵךְ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.17, byte tier) and holds it to MT 2:25, turns to masculine singular with a vocative at וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ ... יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28, byte tier), then to plural at כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.29, byte tier) and again at MT 2:30. Participant shift is a licensed cut class, and the second of these turns falls exactly at the setumah the row disclosed and then dismissed as accompanied by nothing. Imperative forms also stand inside the span at וּדְעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19), רְאִ֤י דַרְכֵּךְ֙ בַּגַּ֔יְא דְּעִ֖י (oshb:Jer.2.23) and מִנְעִ֤י רַגְלֵךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.25), all byte tier - content imperatives inside the address rather than fresh discourse frames, so the tier-1 class name the row uses is defensible while the sentence as written is not. Onset warrant, upheld: the row's own stated ground is a shift into a run of rhetorical questions, which is not a member of the tier-1 signal set, so a seventeen-verse span opens with no named tier-1 device. One refinement to the rival: closing at MT 2:29 on its closure formula is weaker than framed, because closure corroboration operates only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows and MT 2:30 supplies none; the gap in the rejected-alternative field is nonetheless real, and the stronger unweighed rival is the participant-shift seam at MT 2:28 / MT 2:29. Title stack, upheld: the bytes give נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.2.19, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier) but נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Jer.2.22, byte tier; sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier) without the hosts element, so the later site is the lone member of the four-site object lacking it; the row's single parenthesised label covers both sites, drops the postpositive element that makes the shape a closure formula, and supplies no splice for either - a blended count object.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: add variant-note disclosure for MT 2:15, 2:16, 2:20, 2:24, 2:25 and 2:27 (single-witness), and the paseq seg at MT 2:24 as count-only; split the title-stack sentence into its two objects, each with its own byte-tier splice from source under its own oshb: ref, the postpositive element retained, and each with its own digit and tier. boundary_rationale: replace the blanket denial with the per-term disposition the bytes support - no word-event formula and no messenger formula inside the span; imperative forms present at MT 2:19, 2:23 and 2:25 but not discourse frames; participant shifts present at MT 2:28 and MT 2:29 and dispositioned - and state the onset's warrant class explicitly as a non-tier-1 rhetorical-mode shift. strongest_rejected_alternative: add the participant-shift rival at MT 2:28 / MT 2:29, noting the coinciding setumah and the closure formula at MT 2:29, in place of or beside the metaphor-shift rivals. confidence: with no tier-1 device at the onset over a seventeen-verse span, hold at medium_low. Any change to the span itself is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption and is not author work. Test the cure must pass: the mark-disclosure sweep returns clean for variants and paseq across Jer.2.14-Jer.2.30; every negative sentence survives a byte sweep of the span; each stack object carries its own splice, tier and digit - the three tests that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's stated warrant for its close improperly leans on the chapter division, which is never boundary evidence; and the onset warrant turns on an unquoted original-language shape-parallel, the variant note inside the span goes undisclosed, and a byte-true device crosses the rear seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The tier-4 item is upheld outright: the rationale says the close relies on the chapter boundary together with the topic shift, and the notes field repeats that the boundaries are argued from the imperative and the chapter close alone. Chapter division is tier-4 metadata and is never boundary evidence in either direction, so a field that makes it a co-warrant is defective irrespective of where the seam falls. The disclosure item is upheld: MT 2:33 carries a variant note, למדתי לִמַּ֖דְתְּ (oshb:Jer.2.33, byte tier), unpointed beside pointed, and the row argues that verse in prose and lists it as evidence with no disclosure; the row's parashah statement is otherwise exactly right - the layer is silent across MT 2:30-2:37 and the absence is correctly not read as counterevidence. The cross-seam item is upheld in substance and its digit refuted: שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35, byte tier) carries the return root two verses before this unit's close, on a seam whose next unit is built on that root, and the sentence saying the inventories carry nothing further leaves it undisclosed - a device straddling the seam argues continuity against the row unless disclosed. But no single contiguous consonantal object returns the two verses the challenge claims for its anger-turning idiom: that pair stands at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier) and the comparandum clause at MT 4:8 stands at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton tier); a two-verse count across two different spellings is a semantic-class count presented as a skeleton sweep, which the count discipline bars. The shape-parallel item is refined rather than upheld: the row does not claim one lexeme - it names a see-imperative and a hear-imperative and claims the same discourse-frame shape, imperative plus the word-of-YHWH as object, which is byte-true at both sites, שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) and רְא֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier). What is defective is that this original-language construction claim, and the rejected alternative resting on it, cite the comparandum only under a translation ref with no witness splice and no tier, and name no swept object or digit; swept separately the hear-construction stands at 10 verses and the see-construction at 1 verse, skeleton tier, and both of those digits reproduce for the objects named.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: strike the chapter boundary from the close warrant and either re-warrant the close on content alone or state plainly that no content warrant closes the unit and carry the reduced confidence on that basis; add a byte-tier splice under oshb:Jer.2.4 for the comparandum and re-cut the shape claim so it names its object (imperative plus the word-of-YHWH as object) with per-lexeme digits and tier. device_notes: strike the appeal to the chapter close; add variant-note disclosure at oshb:Jer.2.33 (single-witness); add the cross-seam disclosure of the return-root form at oshb:Jer.2.35 with its own named object and digit, and do not carry a two-verse idiom count. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the renewed-onset argument so it names the swept construction and its digit. Any respan is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption. Test the cure must pass: no tier-4 appeal survives in any field; every original-language shape claim carries a byte-tier splice under its own witness ref; every digit reproduces for the object its own sentence names; the mark-disclosure sweep is clean for variants across Jer.2.31-Jer.2.37 - the four tests that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The notes field drifts into process register with an unanchored positional row-count reference and an editorial-methodology statement; and a spelling-bound substring digit is presented as a root count carrying a book-wide earliest claim the bytes refute, while the onset argument leaves the verse's opening word and its closing formula unengaged and three of the span's five verses carry undisclosed variant notes.
rulings.grounds: The count-object defect is upheld and is the heaviest item. The digit reproduces exactly for the contiguous consonantal run of the plene spelling (sweep: 41 verses, skeleton tier, earliest at Jer.3.1), but the sentence carrying it names its object as the return root, and that needle is spelling-bound: the root stands earlier in the immediately preceding material at וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19, byte tier), יְשִׁיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Jer.2.24, byte tier) and שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ (oshb:Jer.2.35, byte tier). The earliest-in-the-book claim is therefore false at the level asserted, and an exclusivity claim is never dampened by naming a tier. Support-audit note: the same digit is reproducible for that needle, so reproducing it is not a check of the object - the object is what fails. The onset item is upheld: MT 3:1 opens on לֵאמֹ֡ר (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier), a bound speech-frame infinitive with no governing verb of speaking anywhere in the verse, and the same verse closes נְאֻם יְהֹוָֽה (oshb:Jer.3.1, byte tier). A verse-initial bound speech frame with no governing verb is a byte-true element sitting exactly at the seam and arguing dependence on what precedes, and the closing formula is a closure shape at the end of the span's opening verse; the row engages neither while resting its onset on the absence of a formula of its own. The disclosure item is upheld: MT 3:2, MT 3:4 and MT 3:5 each carry a variant note and none is disclosed, although the parashah layer was plainly read at MT 3:5, where the petuchah citation is correct as to type and verse and the layer is indeed silent inside MT 3:1-3:4 and at the front seam; no paseq seg falls anywhere in this chapter, so nothing is owed there. The register items are upheld: naming the following three units is a bare positional and count-based cross-row reference where the rule requires verse anchors, and the appeal to a held posture on the cluster's edges narrates an editorial stance rather than a feature of the text. New finding in the same sentence: it also places the cluster's close at Jer.4.4 and calls that this span's close, while this unit's span closes at Jer.3.5 - the self-reference is factually wrong as well as positional. The extent item is refined: the observation behind it is byte-true, since return-root forms stand at MT 2:35 before the claimed cluster and at MT 4:8 after it, but the two-verse skeleton digit offered for it does not reproduce for any single object.
